title: Engine squeals on startup
h1: Why does my car squeal when I start it or turn the wheel?
metaDesc: Engine squealing on startup or when turning the wheel? Find out if it's a slipping belt, tensioner, pulley or power steering, how urgent it is, and what to do.
synonyms: squeal when I start my car
squeal when turning the steering wheel
car squeels when I turn the wheel
intro: A squeal from under the hood at startup, or when you turn the wheel or switch on the A/C, is usually a drive belt slipping on its pulleys. Often it's a simple fix, but the same belt can run the charging system, power steering and water pump. Answer the questions below to see how urgent it is.
safety: If the temperature gauge climbs toward red or you see steam, pull over and turn the engine off.
If the steering suddenly gets very heavy while driving, slow down and pull over safely.
Never reach near the belt or pulleys while the engine is running.

q_other_signs.q: Along with the squeal, is any of this happening?
q_other_signs.help: The drive belt (often called the serpentine belt) is the long ribbed rubber belt on the front or side of the engine. On many cars it turns the alternator, power steering pump and water pump.

opts.a: The temperature gauge is climbing, or the steering suddenly got heavy
The battery warning light is on, or the lights are dimming
A slapping or flapping sound, or the belt looks frayed or has pieces missing
For a few seconds on a cold start, then it goes quiet
When I turn the steering wheel, especially at full lock or while parking
When the A/C or defroster turns on
When I rev the engine or accelerate hard
All the time: a steady squeal, chirp or squeak while the engine runs
Only in wet weather or after driving through puddles

result.title: The drive belt may have broken or come off
result.now: Pull over safely and turn the engine off. Have the car towed, or have a mobile mechanic come to you.
if: If you see steam or the gauge is in the red, don't open the radiator cap. Hot coolant can burn you.
If the belt is still in place but the engine overheated, tell the shop. The water pump or cooling system may also need checking.
If you smell burning rubber or see smoke from under the hood, pull over and turn the engine off.
result.why: On many engines the same belt drives the water pump and power steering. If it slips badly or comes off, the engine can overheat within minutes and steering gets very heavy. Driving on can cause serious engine damage.

causes.name: Broken or thrown drive belt
causes.clues: The squeal stopped suddenly, then the gauge rose or steering got heavy.

causes.name: Failed tensioner or pulley
causes.clues: A rattle or grinding came before the belt failed.

causes.name: Seized water pump or accessory
causes.clues: A loud squeal that never let up before the belt failed.

you: With the engine off and cooled down, look at whether the belt is still on its pulleys.
shop: Accessory bearing check (water pump, alternator, power steering pump)
Cooling system pressure test if it overheated

result.title: The belt may be slipping on the alternator, so the battery may not be charging
result.now: Get it checked within a day. Keep driving to a minimum, turn off accessories like the heated seats and radio, and watch the temperature gauge.
if: If the temperature gauge rises or the steering gets heavy, pull over and turn the engine off. The belt may have come off.
If the lights keep dimming or the dash flickers, the car could die on the road. Don't drive it; have it towed.
If you smell burning rubber or see smoke from under the hood, pull over and turn the engine off.
result.why: The alternator recharges the battery, and it's turned by the drive belt. A squeal plus the battery light often means the belt is slipping or the alternator is struggling. If so, the car is running on battery power, which won't last long. A shop will usually test charging output and the belt tension before replacing the alternator.

causes.name: Worn or loose drive belt
causes.clues: A squeal that's been getting worse, and a shiny or cracked belt.

causes.name: Weak belt tensioner
causes.clues: The tensioner arm bounces or shakes while the engine idles.

causes.name: Failing alternator
causes.clues: A whining or grinding from the alternator, or the battery light comes and goes.

you: With the engine off, look for cracks, shiny glazing or fraying on the belt.
Have the battery and alternator tested. Many parts stores do this free.

result.title: The belt may be coming apart, or a pulley may be failing
result.now: Turn the engine off. Have the car towed, or have a mobile mechanic inspect and repair it where it's parked.
if: If a piece of belt is missing, ask the shop to check that it didn't get caught behind a pulley or cover.
If you smell burning rubber or see smoke, keep the engine off and stay clear of the engine bay until it cools.
result.why: A frayed or slapping belt can come off at any moment, taking out charging, power steering and often cooling at once. A loose strand can also wrap around other parts and damage them.

causes.name: Worn-out belt
causes.clues: Cracks across the ribs, missing chunks or loose threads.

causes.name: Misaligned or wobbling pulley
causes.clues: The belt edge is chewed up on one side.

causes.name: Failing tensioner
causes.clues: The tensioner arm jumps around, letting the belt flap.

you: With the engine off, look at the belt from above for missing pieces or fraying.

result.title: The belt may be worn or a bit loose, and slipping until it warms up
result.now: Book a belt and tensioner check when convenient. Mention that it only happens on cold starts.
if: If the squeal lasts longer, gets louder, or the battery light flickers, get it checked soon.
If you see cracks or missing pieces on the belt, have it checked before your next long trip.
If the temperature gauge climbs or the steering suddenly gets heavy, pull over and turn the engine off. The belt may have slipped off, and it often drives the water pump and power steering.
result.why: A cold, stiff belt grips less, and the alternator works hardest right after startup to recharge the battery. If the belt is worn or the tensioner is weak, it slips for a few seconds and squeals. It usually gets worse over time.

causes.name: Worn or glazed drive belt
causes.clues: The belt is several years old, looks shiny on the ribs, or has cracks.

causes.name: Weak automatic tensioner
causes.clues: A new belt still squeals, or the tensioner arm wobbles.

causes.name: Battery that needs a lot of recharging
causes.clues: The car cranks slowly in the morning.

you: With the engine off, look at the belt for cracks, shine or fraying.
Notice whether the squeal is worse on colder or damp mornings.
shop: Water spray test to tell slipping from pulley misalignment

result.title: The power steering may be loading up a slipping belt, or the fluid may be low
result.now: With the engine off, check the power steering fluid level if your car has a reservoir, and book a check when convenient.
if: If the fluid is low, top it up with the type in your owner's manual and look for a leak. Have the leak checked soon, since low fluid means it's going somewhere.
If the steering suddenly gets heavy while driving, slow down, pull over and turn the engine off. Steering takes much more effort without assist.
If the squeal turns into a constant whine or groan, get it checked soon.
If you see fluid dripping onto hot engine or exhaust parts, or smell burning, turn the engine off. Leaking fluid on hot parts is a fire risk.
If your car has electric power steering (no fluid reservoir), the noise likely isn't the steering pump. Have the belt and suspension checked.
result.why: A hydraulic power steering pump is usually turned by the drive belt. Turning the wheel, especially all the way to one side, makes the pump work hardest. A worn belt or low fluid can make it squeal at that moment.

causes.name: Worn or loose drive belt
causes.clues: The squeal happens mostly at full lock, and the belt is old.

causes.name: Low power steering fluid
causes.clues: The reservoir is below the mark, or there's reddish or amber fluid under the front of the car.

causes.name: Failing power steering pump
causes.clues: A whine or groan along with the squeal, even with full fluid.

you: Check the power steering fluid level with the engine off.
Avoid holding the wheel all the way to one side for more than a few seconds.
shop: Power steering fluid and leak check

result.title: The belt may be slipping when the A/C compressor kicks on
result.now: Book a belt and A/C check when convenient. Mention that the squeal starts when the A/C or defroster turns on.
if: If the squeal becomes a grinding or rattling noise with the A/C on, stop using the A/C and get it checked soon.
If you smell burning rubber with the A/C on, turn the A/C off. If the smell continues or you see smoke, pull over and turn the engine off.
If the temperature gauge climbs or the steering suddenly gets heavy, pull over and turn the engine off. The belt may have slipped off, and it often drives the water pump and power steering.
result.why: When the A/C compressor engages, it adds a sudden load to the belt. A worn belt or weak tensioner can slip for a moment and squeal. The defroster often runs the A/C too, which is why it can happen in winter.

causes.name: Worn belt or weak tensioner
causes.clues: A short squeal right as the A/C clicks on.

causes.name: A/C compressor clutch or bearing problem
causes.clues: A grinding or constant noise from the compressor with the A/C on.

causes.name: A/C compressor starting to seize
causes.clues: The squeal is long and loud every time, and the A/C isn't cooling well.

you: Turn the A/C on and off while parked and listen for the squeal to start and stop.
With the engine off, look at the belt for wear.
shop: A/C compressor clutch and bearing check

result.title: The belt may be slipping under load
result.now: Book a belt and tensioner check within the next couple of weeks.
if: If the battery light comes on, get it checked right away.
If the temperature gauge climbs or the steering suddenly gets heavy, pull over and turn the engine off. The belt may have slipped off, and it often drives the water pump and power steering.
If you see cracks or missing pieces, have the belt checked before any long trip.
result.why: Revving the engine makes the belt speed up quickly, and accessories resist that change. A belt that's worn, stretched or not held tight enough slips briefly and squeals.

causes.name: Worn or stretched belt
causes.clues: The belt is old, shiny or cracked.

causes.name: Weak tensioner
causes.clues: The tensioner arm jumps when you rev the engine.

causes.name: Oil or coolant on the belt
causes.clues: Wet spots or residue near the belt, or a leak at the front of the engine.

you: With the engine off, look for cracks, shine or oily residue on the belt.

result.title: A pulley, tensioner or accessory bearing may be wearing out
result.now: Get it checked within a few days. Keep trips short until then.
if: If the noise turns into a grinding or rattling, or the battery light or temperature gauge changes, stop driving and have it towed.
If the noise is a regular chirp rather than a squeal, a misaligned pulley is possible. Still get it checked soon.
If you smell burning rubber or see smoke from under the hood, pull over and turn the engine off.
result.why: A squeal or chirp that never stops usually isn't just a cold belt. A pulley or bearing that's starting to drag, or a pulley that's out of line, makes the belt squeal constantly. If that bearing seizes, the belt can come off.

causes.name: Worn idler or tensioner pulley bearing
causes.clues: A squeal or growl that's steady at idle.

causes.name: Misaligned pulley
causes.clues: A regular chirp, and one edge of the belt is worn.

causes.name: Failing accessory bearing (alternator, water pump, A/C)
causes.clues: The noise is loudest near one part of the engine.

you: With the engine off, look for uneven wear on one edge of the belt.
Look under the car for coolant drips near the front of the engine.
shop: Engine-running stethoscope check of each pulley

result.title: Water on the belt may be making it slip for a moment
result.now: If it clears up within a few minutes once the belt dries, it's often just water on the belt. Keep an ear on it and mention it at your next service.
if: If it squeals for more than a few minutes, or also on dry days, book a belt check.
If the battery light comes on, get it checked soon.
If the temperature gauge climbs or the steering suddenly gets heavy, pull over and turn the engine off. The belt may have slipped off, and it often drives the water pump and power steering.
result.why: Water reduces the grip between the belt and pulleys, so it can slip and squeal briefly after rain or puddles. A belt in good shape usually goes quiet once it dries. A worn belt gets noisier in wet weather first.

causes.name: Water splashed on the belt
causes.clues: Only after puddles or heavy rain, and it stops once dry.

causes.name: Worn belt that slips easily
causes.clues: The belt is old, and the squeal is getting longer each time.

you: Notice how long the squeal lasts.
With the engine off, check the belt for cracks or shine.
shop: Belt and tensioner inspection if it continues

result.title: Often a drive belt that needs a check
result.now: Book a belt and tensioner check when convenient. Note when the squeal happens so you can tell the shop.
if: If the battery light comes on, the temperature gauge climbs, or the steering gets heavy, stop driving and have it checked right away.
If you smell burning rubber or see smoke from under the hood, pull over and turn the engine off.
result.why: Many squeals from under the hood come from the drive belt slipping or a pulley wearing out. An inspection can usually pinpoint which part is making the noise.

causes.name: Worn or loose drive belt
causes.clues: The belt is old or looks shiny or cracked.

causes.name: Weak tensioner or worn pulley
causes.clues: The squeal is steady, or a new belt didn't fix it.

causes.name: Power steering or A/C load
causes.clues: It happens when turning or with the A/C on.

you: Record a short video with sound when it happens. It helps the shop.
